hints: Look carefully at the tallest bar in P and in Q. P has most elastic tissue, Q has most muscle tissue, and R has the smallest total amount of tissue overall.
Remember the jobs: vessels close to the heart need lots of stretch and recoil, vessels that control blood distribution need lots of contraction, and low pressure vessels have thin walls.
walkthrough:
**Read the bar charts**

Look at what is most abundant in each vessel. P has a very tall elastic bar and a medium muscle bar. Q has a medium elastic bar and a tall muscle bar. R has low amounts of all three tissues, with muscle slightly highest.

Also notice endothelial tissue (white bar) is low and similar in all three, as it is just the thin lining.

**Link tissue to function**

Elastic tissue allows stretch and recoil to smooth out high pressure pulses. Muscle tissue allows contraction and vasoconstriction to control blood flow and pressure.

So: most elastic means elastic artery, most muscle means muscular artery, thinnest wall overall means vein.

**Match P, Q and R**

P with most elastic is the elastic artery. Q with most muscle is the muscular artery. R with the lowest total quantity is the vein. That matches row A.

options.A: Correct. P is elastic artery (most elastic), Q is muscular artery (most muscle), R is vein (thinnest wall, least tissue).
options.B: Incorrect. R cannot be a muscular artery as it has the least muscle and least total tissue, and P cannot be a vein as it has the thickest, most elastic wall.
options.C: Incorrect. P has more elastic than muscle, so it is not a muscular artery, and Q has more muscle than elastic, so it is not an elastic artery.
options.D: Incorrect. Q has a thick wall with lots of muscle, so it cannot be a thin-walled vein, and R has too little tissue to be a muscular artery.
